title: Yogurt, Live
text: {partner} stopped at the store on the way home. Alone. It should be fine.

messages.text: one cow is wearing a hat

outcomes.text: They buy the hat cow. You both knew they would. {kid} takes one bite, says "HAT," and pushes it away forever.
They get it right. First try. {kid} eats two. You feel a love for {partner} that is at least 60% dairy.

choices.label: Video call. Be air traffic control.

outcomes.text: "Left. Your other left. Lower. LOWER." A stranger in a fleece starts helping. The stranger is now on the call. Together, the three of you find it.
{kid} sees the yogurt wall on your screen and screams the name of a yogurt you've never heard of. {partner} buys it. It's correct.
They come home with a $7.99 "drinkable kefir experience" and four tubs of the hat cow. They're so proud. {kid} rejects all of it, on the record.
They come home with no yogurt at all. "It felt like a test," they explain. It was a test.

title: "lol this is us"
text: {partner} sends a meme from work. You study it for a long time.

messages.text: [meme: one parent asleep on a couch, the other holding a baby, a laundry basket and a small fire]

outcomes.text: Typing. Stops. Typing. Stops. It's a good answer. It is not an answer.
They've always known. At 4:52 their car pulls in, early, with noodles.

choices.label: Send a photo: you, {kid}, laundry, chaos

outcomes.text: You, {kid} on your hip, a laundry basket and a pot of pasta foaming over the side. No fire. Close enough.

choices.label: Circle the couch one. Label it YOU.

outcomes.text: They circle the couch one too and label it SATURDAY. You did nap Saturday. For two hours. In a hammock. Ceasefire.
No reply for an hour. Then a screenshot of their calendar: Sunday, 2 to 5 PM, blocked out as COUCH (YOU).

title: Running 20 Late!!
text: A text from {partner}. You can hear the exclamation points from here.

messages.text: it was a meeting about meetings

outcomes.text: Two exclamation points back: the universal sign of a parent doing their best. Twenty minutes is forty. You knew that when you typed it.
{kid} saw you type. "IS IT THEM?" Every ninety seconds for twenty minutes, then for forty.
The period lands like a dropped plate. They walk in twenty minutes later already apologizing, holding gas-station flowers.
They're home in eleven minutes. Nobody has ever driven a period that fast.
They walk in with dumplings and a guilty face. You would take this deal every night of the week.
They forget. They walk in with apologies and a work bag and nothing that can be eaten.

title: Who Booked the Sitter?
text: A thought arrives in two buildings at once.

messages.text: u booked the sitter for friday right
i thought YOU booked the sitter

outcomes.text: Kaylee was already booked. By you. On Monday. You don't remember doing it. Your phone does. Past you is a stranger, and a great one.
Kaylee's free. The backup's free. You each book one. On Friday at 7, two teenagers arrive and $44 an hour leaves the house.

choices.label: "This is a sign. We stay home."

outcomes.text: You both feel relieved. Then terrible about feeling relieved. Then relieved again.
They book Kaylee from a stairwell in nine seconds. Date night survives on {partner}'s grit alone.
You both scroll back eight months to see who booked last time. It was Grandma. The sitter is still unbooked. The scrolling continues.
Mid-argument, Kaylee texts you both: "still on for fri? 🙂" Someone booked Kaylee. Neither of you will ever concede it was the other.

title: Status: In the Bathroom
text: {partner} has been in the bathroom for 26 minutes. Your phone buzzes. It's {partner}. From the bathroom.

messages.text: [link: "Why Parents Need More Time to Themselves"]

outcomes.text: {kid} knocks for four minutes straight: "WHAT ARE YOU DOING. ARE YOU DONE. CAN I SEE." The door opens at minute five. Article: finished.
{kid} knocks, is let in, and doesn't come out. You hear laughing. The bathroom is a club now. You're not in the club, and it's wonderful.

choices.label: Reply with an article of your own

outcomes.text: It exists. Of course it exists. They're out in forty seconds, laughing, and take {kid} for the rest of the evening.

chat.text: [link: "Signs Your Partner Is Hiding in the Bathroom"]

outcomes.text: They reply "lol" and send another article. It's been 31 minutes. Through the door you hear the little noise a phone game makes when you win.

chat.text: [link: "Signs Your Partner Is Hiding in the Bathroom"]

choices.label: Take {kid} to the park. Leave them in there.

outcomes.text: Forty minutes, two swings, one slide, slightly wet. When you get back, {partner} is still in there. They've read eleven articles. They come out rested and extremely sorry.

title: Pink Eye: The Investigation
text: Daycare is closed for pink eye. The group chat has opened an investigation.

messages.text: not to point fingers but someone's little one was rubbing their eyes at pickup friday 👀
it was the kid in the yellow raincoat

outcomes.text: Into the back of the closet, behind the winter coats. Nobody can prove anything. {kid} spends the afternoon asking for "MY YELLOW."
Too late. Brynn posts a photo from Friday pickup: {kid}. Yellow. Both fists in both eyes.
Four parents reply with photos of their kids' raincoats. All navy. Dev's is also navy. Dev says, "lol same."
Marcus: "ours is yellow too." Relief. Then Brynn: "Marcus. 🙂" The investigation turns. You are free.

choices.label: "who had the class turtle last weekend?"

outcomes.text: Fourteen people pivot instantly. A new suspect: the turtle. Brynn proposes a "turtle pause." You've saved {kid} and doomed a turtle.
"the turtle was with US," Brynn writes. "the turtle is FINE." Then Brynn leaves the chat. Then Brynn re-adds Brynn.

title: The Secret Gift Chat
text: You've been added to a new group. It has 22 members: the class chat, minus one. The one is Ms. Patty.

messages.text: hi all!! collecting for Ms. Patty's appreciation basket 💐
$40/family: a candle, a robe and a journal that says GROW 🌱
is that per kid or per family

outcomes.text: Sent. Brynn reacts with a 🙏 in under a second. You're in good standing for $40, which is about what good standing costs.
You send $40. Dev sends $400. Dev meant $40. By the time anyone notices, Brynn has bought a second robe.

choices.label: "what if the gift is just a nap"

outcomes.text: Eleven hearts, fast. It's the most popular thing you've ever said. Then Brynn: "love the energy!! still $40 🙂"
Nobody can argue with that. Nobody tries. You have been out-Brynned.

chat.text: naps aren't a gift, they're a right 🙂

outcomes.text: "You left the conversation." Everyone sees it. There is no quietly. Within a minute, Brynn has messaged you privately.

title: Dev Is Typing
text: Dev, who has only ever written "lol same," is typing. Still typing. Still typing.

messages.text: honestly not doing great. bodhi has been up at 4:10 every day for 2 weeks and yesterday i cried in a car wash

choices.label: DM Dev: "want to get coffee? mine's up at 5 too"

outcomes.text: Dev replies in four seconds. On Thursday you have coffee with someone you've only ever known as two words. They have a lot more words. So do you.
A minute later, one more message. You know exactly what it means now.

chat.text: can't this week, bodhi. but thank you. really

outcomes.text: You type it and mean it. Dev hearts it instantly. It's the most anyone has said in this chat all year.
You send it. Then Marcus: "honestly same." Then Brynn: "same 💛" Dev sends one crying face. It's a good crying face.
A heart from you, one from Marcus, and the chat moves on to a lost water bottle. You meant to say more. You think about the car wash in the shower that night.

title: Daily Report
text: The daycare app pings. Ms. Patty has filed today's report.

messages.text: Lunch: crackers, half a pear, one crayon (tip only) 🖍️
Also {kid} called me {me} three times today! So sweet 🙂

choices.label: "Ha! They call the mail carrier that too 🙂"

outcomes.text: Ms. Patty sends a 😂. Your position in the hierarchy is secure, right alongside the mail carrier, which is fine. It's fine.
So it's just you and Ms. Patty. You and Ms. Patty, sharing a title.

chat.text: Oh, they call the mail carrier "Big Mail" 🙂

outcomes.text: You realize you're more relieved about the crayon than about anything else in the report.
The rest of the crayon is in the backpack, wrapped in a paper towel. It's yours now. You keep it in the car.

choices.label: Pick up early. Reclaim the title.

outcomes.text: {kid} looks up from the sand table: "Hi, {me}." Then, cheerfully, to Ms. Patty: "Bye, {me}." A tie, officially.
You arrive 40 minutes early. {kid} is mid-song, holds up one finger and makes you wait in the doorway like a delivery. You wait. Proudly.

title: Barnaby Bear's Journal
text: Barnaby, the class bear, is coming home with {kid} tonight. Barnaby has a journal. The journal is a competition.

messages.text: Barnaby is coming home with {kid} tonight!! 🐻📓 Please document Barnaby's adventures!
Last week Barnaby went to a lighthouse, an apple orchard and a sound bath with Juniper's family 🌿

choices.label: Stage an adventure. Your kitchen is a market now.

outcomes.text: Barnaby at the "farmers market" (three apples on the counter). Barnaby "hiking" (the stairs). Brynn comments on the journal photo: "love the farmhouse vibe!" It's your kitchen.
{kid} insists Barnaby join bath time. Barnaby goes back to daycare 30% heavier and smelling of strawberry. The entry says "Barnaby swam!"

choices.label: Write the truth: "We had cereal for dinner."

outcomes.text: Ms. Patty reads it aloud at circle time. The parents at pickup laugh. Next week's entry, from Marcus: "Barnaby sat in traffic." Honesty is catching.
Brynn reposts your entry to the group chat with "haha love this 😅". You'll be decoding that sweat drop for weeks.
The library, the duck pond and a fire truck that happened to be parked. Barnaby has the best night of anyone's life. {kid} talks about it through dinner, with Barnaby at the table in a napkin.

title: "quick sync?"
text: Your boss, Trent, has sent two words and a question mark. The report is due at 5.

outcomes.text: Trent wants to "align on fonts." Thirty minutes on fonts. The report due at 5 is now due at 5 minus thirty minutes, in a better font.
It really is nothing bad. Trent just wanted to say "great work lately." You've never been so tired by good news.
Then nothing. The email never comes. You're free, technically. You'll be thinking about "well" until Thursday.
A sentence that means nothing and has put you on a call in two minutes.

chat.text: it's kind of a sync thing

choices.label: "In a meeting! 2pm?" (The meeting is a muffin.)

outcomes.text: The muffin is excellent. The dread is also excellent. It grows all afternoon.

title: Bumping This 🙂
text: Trent has bumped the message. A bump is a knock you can't pretend you didn't hear.

choices.label: Call now. Get it over with.

outcomes.text: It's about the report. It's due at 5. You knew that. Trent knew you knew. Now you both know that Trent knows you know.
Trent wants to know if the report can "also be a deck." You say yes in a voice you don't recognize.
You feel great for four seconds, until you remember {kid} is at daycare and the emergency is you.
Of course it is. Of course. The emergency is now the report.

chat.text: of course! report still on for 5?

title: "Before You Head Out"
text: Friday. The sitter comes at 7. Trent has thoughts.

messages.text: could you look at something this weekend? no rush

outcomes.text: Trent replies "🙌". You'll do it Sunday night, in the hour you'd have spent being a person. Date night has a guest now: the attachment.
Trent sends the tiny favor. It's 61 slides. One of them is just the word "Thoughts?"

choices.label: "I'm offline this weekend." Send. Don't reread.

outcomes.text: That was it. That was all it ever took. You sit in the car for a full minute, a new person.
You spend forty minutes on "np." No problem? Noted, problem? It follows you to the restaurant and sits between you and {partner} like a third diner.

choices.label: Leave it on read until Monday

outcomes.text: "Read." The read receipt does all the talking. Trent will remember. Trent has a folder.
